Crypto lending startup Nimbus and its CEO charged with fraud by the SEC

Published 2026-10-06 16:10 UTC

Nimbus, the crypto lending startup that raised $85 million from venture investors in 2024, has been charged with fraud by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, along with its founder and CEO Mark Ellery.

The SEC alleges Nimbus took in about $1.2 billion from more than 90,000 retail investors through its Yield Vault product, promising returns of up to 14%, and used new deposits to pay earlier users. Ellery is accused of diverting more than $40 million to fund a luxury lifestyle.

Nimbus had pitched itself as a safer, compliant alternative to the lenders that collapsed in 2022. It paused withdrawals in August, citing market conditions. The SEC is seeking disgorgement, penalties and a ban on Ellery serving as an officer of a public company.
